#StartupSpotlight | ManasAI Technology Private Limited | IIT Mandi Catalyst

ManasAI Technology Private Limited, founded by Dr. Jyotiranjan Beuria (Founder), AKASH SHARMA (Co-Founder), and Inderjeet Nagpal (Co-Founder), is an IIT Mandi Catalyst-incubated startup. It is a research-driven company developing systems to sense and model inner well-being and understand the dynamics of the mind, without reducing individuals to mere dashboards or scores.

At the heart of its technology is a simple yet powerful idea: preserving access to raw data streams. This enables researchers to develop personalised, configurable AI models tailored to the needs of their specific studies or institutions, rather than relying on closed, one-size-fits-all scoring systems.

ManasAI aims to empower researchers with better instruments and greater flexibility to develop models that address individual needs.

What drives ManasAI?

🔹 Affordable, AI-powered devices that provide researchers with access to raw physiological signals, not just summary scores.
🔹 Physics-grounded models designed to reflect real-world dynamics, going beyond performance on benchmarks and leaderboards.
🔹 Consciousness as a scientific pursuit, approached through research rather than rhetoric.
🔹 A research-first philosophy: The device measures; it does not lecture.

Introducing SakshiSense
SakshiSense is the first offering in this technology stack a research-grade ring and wristband programme currently at the prototype and development stage.

Designed initially for research laboratories and centres, it aims to capture physiological signals such as PPG (photoplethysmography), motion, and skin conductance, while keeping the underlying data accessible for further research and analysis.

Through its innovations, ManasAI seeks to give researchers better tools, greater flexibility, and more opportunities to advance personalised research and the broader science of well-being.

Atomberg Technologies, founded by IIT Bombay graduates, has received SEBI approval for its proposed Rs 450 crore IPO.

The consumer appliances maker can now proceed with the next stages of its public offering.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 450 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 7.65 crore shares by existing investors.

The Mumbai-based company filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI on August 20, 2026.

Atomberg's revenue from operations rose 34.8% to Rs 1,293.77 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 959.51 crore in FY25.

However, its net loss widened to Rs 148.88 crore from Rs 117.41 crore during the same period.

Founded in 2012, Atomberg initially built its business around energy-efficient ceiling fans and has since expanded into mixer grinders, water purifiers, juicers and smart locks.
